questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning of Executive' refers to.
questions.a: The executive is the organ of government responsible for the implementation and administration of laws and policies. It comprises all functionaries and institutions that carry out the day-to-day governance of the state.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning of Executive'.
questions.a: The executive is the branch of government that executes or implements the laws made by the legislature and runs the administration of the country.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Meaning of Executive' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Meaning of Executive

concepts.title: Types of Executive: Parliamentary and Presidential

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Types of Executive: Parliamentary and Presidential' refers to.
questions.a: The parliamentary executive is one in which the executive is drawn from and accountable to the legislature, while the presidential executive is one in which the President is separately elected and is not accountable to the legislature.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Types of Executive: Parliamentary and Presidential'.
questions.a: In a parliamentary system the executive is a part of and responsible to the legislature, whereas in a presidential system the executive is independent of and separate from the legislature.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Types of Executive: Parliamentary and Presidential' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Types of Executive

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'President of India' refers to.
questions.a: The President of India is the constitutional head of the Indian State, elected indirectly by an electoral college, who exercises executive powers formally on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'President of India'.
questions.a: The President is the formal or nominal head of the executive who acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers, while real executive power lies with the Prime Minister and the Council.

questions.q: Under which section is 'President of India' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: President of India

concepts.title: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Prime Minister and Council of Ministers' refers to.
questions.a: The Prime Minister is the head of the government and the real executive authority in India, who heads the Council of Ministers that is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha and advises the President in the exercise of executive powers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Prime Minister and Council of Ministers'.
questions.a: The Prime Minister is the most powerful political executive in India; the Council of Ministers, headed by the Prime Minister, is the real executive that actually runs the government.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Prime Minister and Council of Ministers' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Real and Nominal Head' refers to.
questions.a: The nominal head is the constitutional or formal head of the State who holds office and exercises powers in name, while the real head is the actual executive authority who exercises real powers and is responsible for running the government.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Real and Nominal Head'.
questions.a: In India, the President is the nominal head who acts on advice, while the Prime Minister is the real head who actually wields executive power.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Real and Nominal Head' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Real and Nominal Head

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Powers of the President' refers to.
questions.a: The President of India exercises executive, legislative, financial, judicial, diplomatic, and emergency powers as provided by the Constitution, although these powers are exercised on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Powers of the President'.
questions.a: The President's powers are broad and constitutional, covering all major areas of governance, but are exercised formally on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Powers of the President' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Powers of the President

concepts.title: Relationship Between President and Prime Minister

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Relationship Between President and Prime Minister' refers to.
questions.a: The relationship between the President and the Prime Minister is defined by the constitutional principle that the President exercises executive powers on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Relationship Between President and Prime Minister'.
questions.a: The President is the constitutional head who acts on the advice of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers, making the Prime Minister the real executive authority while the President remains the formal head.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Relationship Between President and Prime Minister' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: President and Prime Minister

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Bureaucracy and Civil Services' refers to.
questions.a: Bureaucracy refers to the permanent, professional body of civil servants who assist the political executive in implementing laws, formulating policies, and administering the day-to-day affairs of the government, remaining politically neutral and continuing in office regardless of changes in government.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Bureaucracy and Civil Services'.
questions.a: Bureaucracy is the administrative machinery that provides continuity, expertise, and political neutrality in governance, supporting the political executive in implementing policies.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Bureaucracy and Civil Services' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Bureaucracy and Civil Services
